USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Patient factors and drug response: 5

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

Two otherwise similar patients metabolize the same drug at very different rates. Testing identifies an inherited enzyme variant in one patient. Which patient factor best explains the difference in drug exposure and response?

  1. Rebound effect
  2. Reduced renal elimination
  3. Pharmacogenetic variation
  4. Tolerance
  5. Physical dependence
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Pharmacogenetic variation

Inherited differences in drug metabolism or targets can alter efficacy and toxicity.

Understanding the options

Pharmacogenetic variation
Inherited differences in drug metabolism or targets can alter efficacy and toxicity.
Tolerance
A reduced response after repeated exposure may require more drug for the previous effect; it is not synonymous with addiction. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Physical dependence
Physiological adaptation can produce withdrawal when drug exposure is abruptly reduced. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Rebound effect
Symptoms can temporarily exceed baseline after withdrawal of a suppressive treatment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Reduced renal elimination
Impaired kidney function can raise exposure to a predominantly renally eliminated drug. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
